title: Counting Routine Benefits Against Their Frequency Limits
content:
Each routine benefit under the Optional Supplemental Benefit Riders has its own frequency limit, and the rider pays for it only while the limit still allows it in the benefit year or period the limit is counted on.

## What is counted per benefit year

Cleanings, examinations, radiograph sets and fluoride treatments are counted per benefit year, and the count resets on the first day of the new benefit year whatever was used the year before.

## What is counted on months that must pass

Crowns, dentures, frames and hearing aids are counted on months that must pass since the last one the rider paid for, measured on the same tooth, the same eye or the same ear, so that two crowns on different teeth in one year are both paid.

## Where a limit is reached

A service beyond its limit is denied on the ground that its frequency limit has been reached, and the member is told the exact date from which it would be paid again.

## What does not use up a frequency

A service the rider denied or reversed does not use up a frequency, so a member whose claim was put right does not lose a cleaning they never had.

## Telling a member what is left

A member who asks how many cleanings they have left is told the figure and the date it resets, rather than being sent to their dentist to find out.

## A member who changes rider mid-year

Where a member changes rider part way through a benefit year, the frequencies already used under the old rider count against the new one, because the limit follows the member and not the record.

## Points of judgement

| Question | The basis | The answer |
|---|---|---|
| Two crowns in one year, on different teeth | Crowns are counted on months that must pass on the same tooth | Both are paid |
| A cleaning claimed after the year's count is used | Cleanings are counted per benefit year | The service is beyond its limit and is denied on that ground |
| A cleaning whose claim the rider reversed | A denied or reversed service uses up no frequency | The count stands as though that service had never been paid |
| The first cleaning of a new benefit year, the old year's count having been used | The count resets on the first day of the new benefit year | It is within the limit |
| A member who moved from one rider to another mid-year | The limit follows the member, not the record | What was used under the old rider counts against the new one |
